answer: Each new agent must complete a twenty-minute live uniqueness interview on a booked slot, while a 2,400-unit bond sits in escrow for 16 days. Interviews run at a public mesa station, recorded with a liveness challenge, and checked so the same face, room, or device cannot sponsor a second key. An honest applicant spends one slot and parks 2,400 units. A farm chasing the zenith of voting power with 200 aliases needs 200 distinct people and 480,000 units locked, plus about 67 hours of interview time, more than a shallow reef of airdrop prizes can repay.
